newsitem.title: GERMANY: Rheinmetall gets 24.99 pct of Kolbenschmidt.
newsitem.headline: Rheinmetall gets 24.99 pct of Kolbenschmidt.

text.p: Germany's Rheinmetall AG said on Wednesday that, pending the agreement of the supervisory board of Commerzbank AG, it would buy the bank's 24.99 percent stake in car components firm Kolbenschmidt.
British auto components group T&N Plc had also been seeking to purchase a stake in Kolbenschmidt.

Rheinmetall said the deal, which will double its sales to around seven billion marks a year and which had the backing of Kolbenschmidt itself, was part of a move to gain a position of management control within Kolbenschmidt.
It added in a statement that it planned this year further "steps towards industrial solutions" in this connection.
A Rheinmetall spokesman could not immediately say whether such steps could involve proposals to purchase a similar size stake in which T&N is interested.

That stake, which was also formerly held by Commerzbank, was transferred to Germany's Metallbank last December, which in turn parked it with a group of institutional investors, retaining the right to recall the stake if required.
T&N has an option on that stake but has thus far been thwarted in its attempts to gain control in Kolbenschmidt by German cartel authorities.

Rheinmetall, a defence and engineering group, said that this deal and the "consistent development" of its stake in Kolbenschmidt would grow its car component revenues to around 2.8-3.3 billion marks with a pre-tax profit of around 100 million marks.
